notes: Identity independently verified from the document title, Paul W. Eastwick and Eli J. Finkel, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2008, Vol. 94, No. 2, 245–264, and printed DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.94.2.245. This is a full primary research article text with Methods, Results, Discussion and References, not an abstract or secondary report. Supplied provenance line names a PDF URL; no network used. No PDF path was supplied, so no rendering was performed. Only n_o and es_value_o are assigned; replication, p and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Both assigned fields remain target_ambiguous. Page 9/Table 2 has several printed r candidates: physical attractiveness overall r .43 (men) and .46 (women) for speed-date/match, .26 and .31 for write-ins; physical-attractiveness sex-difference r .03 (p = .673) and .05 (p = .499). Earning-prospects overall r .19 and .16 for speed-date/match, .16 and .18 for write-ins; sex-difference r −.04 (p = .480) and .02 (p = .825). Personable overall r .29 and .32 for speed-date/match, .25 and .27 for write-ins; sex-difference r .03 and .02 (p = .714 and .812 on p. 254). Table 2 also prints many outcome-specific unstandardized regression Bs. These are candidates, not assigned target values. The broad sex/preferences/self-knowledge description does not distinguish characteristic, outcome, sample, sex, or association versus sex difference. Method p. 248 reports recruitment of 163 students, 81 women and 82 men; this is not an explicitly established final analytic sample for a uniquely identified test. The analysis strategy p. 251 distinguishes speed-date/match observations nested in participants from follow-up waves nested in matches/write-ins nested in participants. Page 252 describes 28 speed-date/match Bs used in one physical-attractiveness meta-analysis; these are regression coefficients, not 28 participants. Page 249 reports 92% elected follow-up and 69% of those completed at least 9 questionnaires, and 143 write-ins; none establishes an assigned critical-model analytic N. No N was calculated, no df-based N inference was made, and no metric conversion was performed.
